content: {"like":["Respectful and innovative adaptation that created an original work inspired by the novel","The middle section of the film, preserving Jason Compson’s speeches and the romantic despair that contributed to his eldest son’s death","Moments that glimpse what might have been a far better film","The film is far superior to the earlier crass, absurd adaptation by Jerry Wald and Martin Ritt"],"dislike":["Not sufficiently faithful to the novel, with many omitted sections and missing essential elements","Representation of the Compson mansion and other settings that do not reflect the novel’s descriptions","The film’s muddled portrayal of characters such as Quentin and the little Italian girl","Franco’s performance as Benjy, described as self-indulgent, grotesque, and lacking subtlety","The casting of Seth Rogen in a small role, seen as narcissistic","Overall lack of detail, careful observation, and substantive accuracy","The film’s failure to be original enough or risk‑taking compared to Franco’s As I Lay Dying"]}
